svg.title: P002 · Ten highest-priced products
svg.desc: One row per ranked product, up to ten. ID 31 drops out. ID 30 costs zero, which is still a known price. Twelve rows qualify. Nine products cost more than 100. Mug (ID 4) comes before Bottle (ID 20) at the same price. Mug takes place 10. Bottle is 11th and the zero-price Sticker is 12th.
svg.text: One row per ranked product, up to ten.
Mug and Bottle both cost 100. Which one gets the last place?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
Which prices can enter the ranking?
ID 31 drops out. ID 30 costs zero, which is still a known price. Twelve rows qualify.
What separates products tied on price?
Nine products cost more than 100. Mug (ID 4) comes before Bottle (ID 20) at the same price.
ORDER BY Sale_Price DESC, ProductID ASC
Which ten rows reach the report?
Mug takes place 10. Bottle is 11th and the zero-price Sticker is 12th.
